findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when TopicUser row is missing
findings.body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107, TopicsController#unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and then immediately reads tu.notification_level. find_by returns nil when the user has no TopicUser row for that topic, which is common for email recipients who never visited the topic, were emailed via mailing-list mode, or were invited. Dereferencing nil raises NoMethodError and returns 500, so clicking the email unsubscribe link crashes instead of unsubscribing. The code must handle nil via TopicUser.change or find-or-create.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe via GET enables CSRF and prefetch unsubscribes
findings.body: In config/routes.rb:440, the per-topic unsubscribe URL is a GET that maps to TopicsController#unsubscribe, which mutates TopicUser.notification_level on every hit. GET requests have no CSRF token protection and are automatically fetched by browsers, email link prefetchers, antivirus scanners, and crawlers. An attacker can force a logged-in victim to downgrade/mute arbitrary topics with an tag, and legitimate users can be unsubscribed without ever clicking. Mutations must use POST/PUT with authenticity-token protection plus explicit user confirmation.

findings.title: Email unsubscribe link requires login so logged-out recipients cannot use it
findings.body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:28, :unsubscribe is added to ensure_logged_in. Email recipients normally open links without an active Discourse session, so they are redirected to the login page and the TopicUser mutation never runs, and after login they are not replayed through the mutation. The email copy promising 'click here to stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' therefore does nothing for logged-out users. Email unsubscribe needs a signed single-use token usable without a session, like DigestUnsubscribeKey.

findings.title: Direct save bypasses notification-level bookkeeping and live updates
findings.body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113, the action assigns tu.notification_level directly and calls tu.save! instead of using TopicUser.change. That bypasses setting notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id and bypasses the MessageBus publish of notification_level_change that TopicUser.change performs. As a result open topic pages keep stale notification state, tracking-state observers are not run, and audit fields are wrong. The action should use TopicUser.change with an appropriate reason.

findings.title: Client-side unsubscribe route never calls server unsubscribe action
findings.body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6, the Ember model hook loads the topic with PostStream.loadTopicView, which hits the normal topic show API, not TopicsController#unsubscribe. A full page load to /t/slug/id/unsubscribe hits Rails and auto-downgrades the level, but an in-app transition to the same URL only runs this hook and never mutates, while the template still says the user will stop receiving notifications. Behavior depends on navigation path and the displayed text can be false.

findings.title: New unsubscribe_link translation breaks callers without unsubscribe_url
findings.body: In lib/email/message_builder.rb:90, email bodies append I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args). The PR changed server.en.yml unsubscribe_link to require both %{user_preferences_url} and a new %{unsubscribe_url}, but MessageBuilder only supplies user_preferences_url by default; unsubscribe_url is present only if the caller passes it. Any existing caller, plugin, or test that sets add_unsubscribe_link:true without unsubscribe_url now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fails to deliver mail, where it previously succeeded. The template needs a default or separate handling when unsubscribe_url is absent.
